_notes: The indexed-repository fleet standing in for the promotion corpus's
diversity arm. This is the code-side half of the CORPUS, not a stand-in for
any part of the truth core: it supplies the rows completed index runs would
have left behind (repositories + code_files + code_edges), and every
assertion, fact, provenance row and ladder decision downstream of it is
produced by shipped code -- code_deriver.assert_repo_graph,
fact_lift.run_code_lift, verification_recompute.run_recompute. Writing those
three tables by hand is the same act as writing the memory corpus by hand;
what may not be written by hand is what the ladder reads to decide, and
nothing here is.
The imports are all real, published Python packages, none of which is a
stdlib module or a suffix of an indexed file path -- the two conditions
code_deriver.dependency_name / is_internal_import decline on.
T2.129 grew the first repo from 12 edges to one the size a real service of
that shape carries, because the diversity bucket grows one claim per import
and the false-promotion audit is undecidable below 100 corroborations.
T2.131 made it a FLEET of six, because the audit is now scored on the 95%
Clopper-Pearson upper bound and the window that settles it is near 500. The
first repo was claim-saturated at 101 claims against 101 imports, and one
stand-in service carrying several hundred distinct third-party dependencies
is not a repository anyone indexed -- plausibility is the premise the whole
corpus rests on, so the arm had to widen sideways rather than deepen.
THE FLEET'S SHAPE IS ADJUDICATED, not incidental (plan section 0a).
Manufactured-ness is a shape and not a count, so three properties hold and
are asserted by test: at most six repos, none over 101 imports and each new
one between 40 and 90; the siblings SHARE A COMMON CORE, because a fleet of
pairwise-disjoint dependency sets is itself the manufactured signature; and
each repo leaves at least a tenth of its imports UNCLAIMED, because a repo
claiming every import it has is a claim manifest wearing a repo's clothes.
Each repo's dependency set is role-coherent with the service it describes.
EDITING CONSTRAINT: this file is half of the corpus's diversity design.
Every `diversity` claim in corpus.json names one repo here and exactly one
of THAT repo's imports, so removing or renaming a target_key removes that
claim's second origin -- it would still load and run, and would silently
hold at one origin outside the diversity bucket. Both directions are checked
by promotion_corpus.validate_diversity_group_against_fixture; edit the claim
and its import together. Two claims may name one dependency in DIFFERENT
repos -- different subjects are different facts, each seconded by its own
repo's code origin -- and may not in the same repo. An import no claim
mentions is allowed: it mints a code-only fact born on the rung, which the
completeness probe counts as a carve-out rather than losing.
A CLAIMED dependency must also type outside code_deriver's
_USES_ENTITY_TYPES. The deriver asserts USES for a database, service,
protocol or language and DEPENDS_ON for everything else, while a memory
reading 'X depends on Y' lifts DEPENDS_ON -- two rel_types are two
triple_keys and the two origins never meet. That is the measured cause of
two of T2.129's three unconverged claims (`redis` and `elasticsearch`, the
only two of those 101 imports that type that way); both are left as they are
so the 0.9703 conversion constant the sizing reconciles against still
describes the corpus it was measured on.
